summary.text: John Ley is a Republican member of the Washington House of Representatives for District 18-Position 2, in office since January 13, 2025, and he is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Democrat Deken Letinich.
A retired Air Force officer and airline pilot, he worked for Delta Air Lines for more than 31 years.

paragraphs.text: Ley earned an Air Force ROTC scholarship in college, then a commission as a public affairs officer, and secured a pilot slot on his fifth attempt, according to his House Republican biography.
He flew KC-135 tankers during more than 11 years of service, then became a pilot for Delta Air Lines.
After retiring, he spent 20 months as a reporter for Clark County Today.
Ley served five years on the board of directors of the Airline Pilots Association and, after Delta's bankruptcy following the September 11 attacks, started a small business, the biography says.
He succeeded Republican Greg Cheney in the House.

His priorities include transportation, particularly the I-5 Interstate Bridge project, public safety, reducing government overreach and improving student outcomes, and he serves on the Environment and Energy Committee.
